name: Zheng He's fourth voyage reaches East Africa
summary: On his fourth treasure-fleet voyage (1413–1415) under the Yongle Emperor's commission, Zheng He's detached squadrons reach Hormuz, Aden, and Mogadishu. A Mogadishu envoy returns with the fleet to Nanjing, bringing the giraffe that became famous in early-Ming court iconography as the qilin.

_quarry.structural_significance: Earliest documented direct Sino-East African diplomatic contact. The seven Zheng He voyages (1405–1433) projected Ming naval power across the Indian Ocean on a scale never matched in the medieval period; their abrupt termination after Yongle's death exemplifies the early Ming pivot from maritime expansion to continental consolidation.
